originality.rationale: Full motivating source and two closest published mathematical findings concern higher-dimensional partial-plank existence/erosion or minimum-width structure but do not imply the exact comparison between optimally shifted minimum-width and facet-normal one-plank volumes. Actual targeted published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches found no statement giving the two formulas, sharp crossing, or all-minimum-width-normal exclusion. Residual old simplex-spline overlap cannot be excluded.
residual_risks: An exact Beta(2,2) versus Beta(1,3) interval-mass comparison may have appeared in unindexed older simplex-spline or geometric-tomography literature under different terminology.
No claim is made for generic oblique plank normals, so the global one-plank optimum and arbitrary-family optimum remain open under this result.
Relevant broadly titled classical treatments of tetrahedron slicing were not exhaustively inspected; absence from searches is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The simplest 3D regular simplex gives an exact, width-resolved obstruction to the mathematically motivated search restriction to minimum-width orientations in partial-plank capture. The entire strict-loss interval and its crossing are proved, with the underlying 2–2 versus 1–3 vertex partition geometry explaining the effect. The statement is not a routine substitution into a published planar optimum and does not overclaim unrestricted global optimality.
